objective: Make the partially effective candidate-dossier workflow executable by auditing explicit ledger state after broad discovery and separating legal qualification from user-facing output selection.

evidence: debugger/tasks/task-3ae3617271007c9733ea/result.json: an explicit ledger remained unresolved while search snippets became pseudo-evidence
debugger/tasks/task-ce9d336f6a529eed408e/result.json: surfaced candidates were not reconciled into source-resolved rows

changes.failure_pattern: Broad discovery advanced while the agent-authored candidate ledger was absent, unchanged, unparseable, or explicitly unresolved, so plausible matters disappeared before candidate-local review.
changes.mechanism: The registered coverage middleware now fingerprints the scratch ledger, records successful corpus-boundary discovery revisions, parses generic markdown candidate rows, and injects one replaceable bounded reminder when discovery is not checkpointed or rows contain explicit open markers.
changes.rationale: The retained tools already expose bounded discovery and source-aware reads; the earliest recurrent failure is cross-turn state reconciliation, which middleware can inspect deterministically without deciding legal relevance or reviving the harmful lexical finish gate.

changes.failure_pattern: The free-form workflow permitted aggregate or stale rows and conflated source quality, legal qualification, and external answer membership, causing both omitted candidates and comparator overdisclosure.

changes.rationale: The skill remains the appropriate progressively disclosed surface for detailed legal research procedure, while its exact state vocabulary gives the deterministic middleware a reliable audit target and resolves the C6 instruction conflict.
